(a) we propose a light-weight version of RefineNet, which is suitable for real-time performance, (b) we achieve more than a twofold model size reduction with only minor performance degradation, and (c) our model is easily mixable into classification networks.
(i) RefineNet [47] is a powerful semantic segmentation model, (ii) it can be made light-weight, and (iii) it can be used in real-time applications.

(1) RefineNet is a powerful and efficient semantic segmentation architecture, (2) we can significantly speed up RefineNet by removing computationally expensive blocks from the original architecture, and (3) the resulting light-weight model can be easily mixed with light-weight classification architectures to attain even higher performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: 1) we propose two modifications of the RefineNet architecture that reduce the computational burden of the model, 2) we demonstrate that our modifications do not affect the performance of the original RefineNet architecture, 3) we show that our modifications allow for a more efficient training of RefineNet and, as a consequence, 4) we demonstrate that the proposed approach is applicable for the tasks that require real-time semantic image segmentation.

two important aspects: (1) the design of a compact semantic segmentation architecture that is suitable for high-resolution inputs and can achieve real-time performance, and (2) the design of an efficient and effective model that can achieve high performance even with a light-weight backbone network.

we present an approach that can be applied to a wide range of tasks, including semantic segmentation and classification, and that can be used to obtain high performance models with low computational complexity.
our approach is a solid and effective solution for real-time semantic image segmentation, which is able to maintain high levels of performance while being computationally light and efficient.

our approach allows to attain the same performance levels of the original RefineNet [47] with 1.7-2 times less number of parameters, 1.2-2 times less FLOPS, 1.3-2 times less memory consumption, and 1.2 times less inference time.

we provide the community with a new light-weight semantic segmentation model, which is suitable for real-time performance on modern GPU cards, and which can be easily adapted to different tasks.

we provide a new baseline for semantic segmentation on PASCAL, that is, a new model that is faster than all other state-of-the-art methods, but at the same time is also competitive in terms of performance.
we propose a simple and effective way to adapt a state-of-the-art segmentation network into a light-weight one, suitable for real-time tasks.
